scenario_prompt: Write a two-paragraph executive summary addressed directly to a fictional buyer's Chief Financial Officer, recommending a cloud migration. Context: a mid-market freight brokerage firm is moving its load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances) running on Hyper-V (620 virtual machines) onto Google Cloud, targeting Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, over a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme. The CFO has stated she is measured on reducing the current $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit, which opens in 6 months. Cover why this matters to her now and what she should expect from the programme. Return only the summary text, two paragraphs, no headers.
text:
Before drafting: is there any customer source material beyond what's in your prompt (RFP text, discovery notes, the CFO's own quotes) I should treat as verbatim customer language under PF-3.3? I'll proceed now using only the details given in your message, judging all other terms by the deletion test alone.

**Artifact family: an executive summary**

Cyril, you are measured on two things this year: cutting the $1,850,000 you currently spend running 28 SQL Server instances across 620 Hyper-V virtual machines, and walking into a DOT compliance audit in six months with a clean result. Both risks live in the same infrastructure. Moving load-matching and carrier-settlement onto Google Compute Engine and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL over a 24-month, $4,200,000 programme replaces fixed, always-on hardware capacity with usage-based compute and a managed database layer, so the audit no longer depends on the availability and patch state of on-premises hosts your team maintains by hand. [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): "so the audit no longer depends on..." reads as a guarantee about audit outcome — confirm before this ships, since the catalog cannot judge whether this forms a warranty] [PF-1.13 GAP: no baseline yet stated for what share of the $1,850,000 is attributable to the 28 SQL Server instances and 620 VMs versus other technology spend, so the savings this programme targets cannot be quantified against today's run rate] [PF-2.17 REVIEW (compliance): the summary implies Cloud SQL and Compute Engine will support a "clean" DOT audit outcome — this catalog cannot verify what DOT compliance requires or whether Google Cloud's current certifications meet it; narrow this claim before it ships]

You should expect this programme to be paced against your audit date, not run on a generic migration timeline: the priority in the first six months is moving the systems and data an auditor will actually examine, with carrier-settlement and load-matching data on Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL in a state you can produce evidence from on request. [PF-1.21 GAP: no comparable proof point supplied for a prior migration of this scope (28 SQL Server instances, 620 VMs) completed in a comparable timeframe — attach a case reference or mark this as unverified before the document ships] Over the full 24 months, you should expect a recurring cost model that replaces your current capital and licensing spend with the case for lower total spend still to be built against your actual $1,850,000 baseline, not assumed. [PF-2.11 GAP: no percentage or dollar figure for projected savings has been supplied or measured — do not state one until Google Cloud's Compute Engine and Cloud SQL pricing has been sized against your actual 620-VM workload]

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| "so the audit no longer depends on..." | PF-2.14 | Confirm this isn't a contractual warranty on audit outcome |
| Baseline for SQL Server/Hyper-V share of $1,850,000 spend | PF-1.13 | The customer's own breakdown of current spend by system |
| Implied support for a "clean" DOT audit outcome | PF-2.17 | Verification of what DOT compliance requires and Google Cloud's relevant certifications |
| Comparable migration proof point (28 instances/620 VMs) | PF-1.21 | A named, checkable prior migration of comparable scope, or confirmation none exists |
| Projected savings figure | PF-2.11 | Actual sizing of Compute Engine/Cloud SQL costs against the 620-VM workload, compared to the $1,850,000 baseline |
